name: Mohamed Alabbar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Mohamed Alabbar is the founder of  Dubai-based real estate developer Emaar Properties, which built the world's tallest tower, Burj Khalifa.
He founded the firm in 1997 and took it public on the Dubai stock exchange in 2000. He stepped down as chairman in 2020.
Most of Alabbar's fortune comes from his 33% stake in publicly traded Americana Restaurants, which owns fast food franchises in the Middle East.
In 2014, Alabbar founded Eagle Hills in Abu Dhabi, which has developed high-end apartments, hotels and retail in 10 countries on three continents.
Alabbar also owns stakes in Riyadh-based e-commerce platform Noon.com and Dubai-based digital bank Zand Bank.
forbes_facts: The son of a traditional dhow boat captain, Alabbar's first job after college was at the UAE's central bank.

name: Zhang Tao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Tao was the CEO of restaurant review site Dianping when it merged with Groupon-like Meituan in 2015.
Meituan went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Zhang received an MBA from Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania in 2002, and returned to China in 2003, when he set up Dianping.

name: Mark Hancock
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Mark Hancock is the cofounder and executive vice chairman of Utah-based PACS Group, a publicly traded firm that operates skilled nursing facilities.
He cofounded PACS Group with fellow billionaire Jason Murray in 2013 and the pair took the company public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024.
PACS Group started with two skilled nursing facilities and has since expanded to 315 facilities in 17 states in the U.S.
Hancock and Murray each owned 50% of PACS Group before the IPO; Hancock now owns nearly 35% of the company's shares.
Before starting PACS, Hancock worked as an analyst at Ford, as a director at a steel company and as treasurer of a financial services firm.
forbes_facts: In 2024, Hancock's private investment firm PV3 acquired Utah-based bicycle manufacturer ENVE Composites for $20 million.

name: Glenn Dubin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Glenn Dubin cofounded multi-strategy hedge fund Highbridge Capital in 1992.
Dubin sold a majority stake to JPMorgan in 2004 for $1.3 billion.
He also cofounded quantitative hedge fund Engineer's Gate and is the lead shareholder of Castleton Commodities, an energy firm he bought with an investor group that included Paul Tudor Jones in 2012.
Dubin runs a family office, Dubin & Co., which backs early and late-stage growth companies, including Brex and Scale AI.
The first person in his family to attend college, Dubin played football for Stony Brook University before getting a job as a stock broker at EF Hutton.
forbes_facts: Dubin is a founding board member of the Robin Hood Foundation, a New York poverty-fighting group.
Dubin and his wife, Eva, an MD and breast cancer survivor, donated millions to found the Dubin Breast Center at Mount Sinai Medical Center, which opened in 2011.

name: Devi Shetty
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Cardiac surgeon Devi Shetty founded and runs Bangalore-based hospital chain Narayana Health.
It has 47 healthcare facilities including a hospital in the Cayman Islands.
U.K.-trained Shetty founded Narayana Health as Narayana Hrudayalaya in the year 2000.
Shetty took the company public in 2015. Biopharma billionaire Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw has a small stake in the company.
An ardent advocate of affordable healthcare, Shetty helped design the Yeshasvini scheme, a micro-insurance program in his home state of Karnataka.
forbes_facts: He's often seen in his trademark blue surgeon's outfit.
Shetty was Mother Teresa's personal physician.
In November 2025, Narayana Health, inked a deal to acquire UK's Practice Plus Group Hospitals for $248 million.

name: Dmitry Mazepin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: In early 1990s Dmitry Mazepin co-founded a bank, insurance company and petroleum trader.
In 1999-2002 he worked as Deputy Chairman with the state Russian Federal Property Fund.
In 2004 he bought the first fertilizer manufacturer at the privatization auction. Then he founded Uralchem Group and acquired several fertilizer producers in Russia.
Uralchem is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of nitrogen, potash and complex fertilizers.
From 2022 to 2024 Uralchem made several humanitarian shipments of fertilizers to Africa.
Mazepin was sanctioned by EU and U.K. in March 2022.
In 2024 elected as President of Aquatics Federation of Russia.
forbes_facts: Born in Belarus, Mazepin graduated from the Minsk Suvorov Military School.
Son Nikita Mazepin is professional racing driver and former Formula One pilot.

name: Alexandra Andresen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2017)
forbes_bio: Alexandra Andresen and her sister Katharina, one year her senior, each inherited 42% of the family-owned investment company Ferd.
Andresen's father Johan still runs the company and controls 70% of the votes via a dual-class share structure.
Ferd runs hedge funds, is an active investor on the Nordic stock exchange, and has private equity investments.
forbes_facts: Alexandra is a three-time junior Norwegian champion in dressage riding.
The Andresen family has been a household name in Norway for over 100 years, primarily known for its tobacco brand, which they sold in 2005.

name: Zygmunt Solorz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Zygmunt Solorz (formerly Solorz-Zak) founded Polsat, one of the first national commercial broadcasters in the Eastern Europe.
It is now part of his Cyfrowy Polsat, Poland's leading pay-TV operator.
Solorz's business empire includes mobile, energy and financial products.
forbes_facts: Zygmunt Solorz made his first fortune importing used cars from Germany.
Solorz flies planes as a hobby and controls Jest Story, which charters jets in Central Europe.

name: Lin Lairong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Lairong's fortune mainly accrues from his stake in Inner Mongolia Dazhong Mining, an iron ore mining business
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2021.
Dazhong is headquartered in the city of Baotou in Inner Mongolia.

name: Linda Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: A scion of the billionaire Pritzker family, Linda Pritzker devotes herself to Tibetan Buddhism rather than her family's enterprises.
She is building a spiritual retreat center in Montana dedicated to Tibetan Buddhist practice; she offers online courses and annual coastal retreats in the interim.
Her father Robert Pritzker and his brother Jay Pritzker built up manufacturing business Marmon Holdings and sold it to Berkshire Hathaway in 2008.
Pritzker goes by Lama Tsomo in her teaching and professional capacities.
The Pritzker family also built the Hyatt hotel empire.
forbes_facts: Pritzker published a Westerner's guide to Tibetan Buddhist meditation that included an introductory letter from H.H. Dalai Lama.
Pritzker was one of the first American women to be ordained as a Lama in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition.
